title: pact_events: carry the 0.11.0 attribution chain
spec: pact 0.11.0 stamps harness, model, harness_session, harness_subagent, branch on every event
acceptance: Event carries harness, model, harness_session, harness_subagent and branch, every one Option — a pre-0.11.0 ledger must still parse, because recount's own 0.0.1 ledger is one and is un-keyed forever. Unknown fields still ignored; chain_hash still ignored for the same reason as before. Tested against THIS repo's live ledger, which now has rows both with and without the chain, and against the 0.0.1-era rows that have none.

title: model: a confidence TIER, so an answer says how it was reached
spec: Confidence "keyed"; ladder order keyed > topological, both always reporting which tier answered and why the higher one did not
acceptance: A Tier type distinguishes a keyed answer from a topological one, and Confidence can express `keyed` rather than a score pretending to be one — a keyed hit is an identity, not a 0.97. Evidence gains a Signal for the keyed filename. Serde round-trip test. The existing four-rung topological ladder is untouched: this bead adds a tier above it, it does not renumber it.

title: claude_code: resolve a transcript by subagent id, and expose the model it recorded
spec: resolve the transcript by FILENAME (subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl): exact match ... does the session schema expose the model per turn?
acceptance:
Given a harness_session and a harness_subagent, produce the transcript path WITHOUT scanning: it is one join of known components plus a stat. Absent file is a distinct outcome from a malformed id, because the join must tell 'pruned or foreign machine' from 'nonsense'.

SECOND HALF, empirical: determine whether the session schema records the model PER TURN, and if so expose it on the turn or the meta. docs/format-notes.md gets the finding either way, dated, with the drift warning. If the schema does not expose it, say so and the comparison bead degrades silently — never an error for a comparison that cannot be made.

title: join: the keyed tier, above the topological one
spec: when a pact event carries harness_subagent, resolve the transcript by FILENAME: exact match, Confidence "keyed", evidence = the filename; ladder order keyed > topological
acceptance:
A keyed hit answers with Tier::Keyed, confidence `keyed`, and evidence naming the filename that proved it — no scoring, no candidates, no tie to break. Falls through to the topological ladder when the event carries no harness_subagent, and the result ALWAYS says which tier answered and, when it was the lower one, why the higher one did not apply.

NEW REFUSAL, distinct from no-cwd-match: a keyed id present whose file is absent. The message must name the two real causes — the worktree/transcript was pruned, or this ledger came from another machine — because that is the difference between 'look harder here' and 'you cannot answer this here at all'.

This bead also closes recount-gwx if the keyed tier makes it moot for keyed events; say explicitly whether it does, and if the topological tie-break bug survives for un-keyed events, say that too.

title: at: the testimony header names the full chain
spec: the testimony header names the full chain ... print agreement or a discrepancy line
acceptance:
`at` renders harness, model with its `(declared)` marker, harness_session, harness_subagent and branch from the event in question, plus which tier answered. Model comparison: when the session records a model, print agreement or a discrepancy line naming both sides ('declared X, session records Y — orchestration drift'); when it does not, print nothing about it and never error.

Output shape changes, so the cli-surface gate applies IN THIS BEAD: --help, docs/cli.md and the generated completions reconciled, `scripts/check-docs.sh` green.

title: explain: same chain, same comparison, inherited not reimplemented
acceptance: `explain` passes the event's harness_subagent into the join so the keyed tier can fire — that is the whole point of explain, since it is the command that HAS the event. It keeps calling at::run_with rather than reimplementing anything. Exit codes unchanged. Surface reconciled in this bead if anything user-visible moved.

title: sessions: an identity that is known, not guessed
acceptance: Where a transcript's id appears as harness_subagent in the repo's ledger, `sessions` reports the identity as KNOWN and names the event that proves it — not as a `fleet_identity_guess` with a confidence. The guess machinery stays for un-keyed sessions and must keep saying it is a guess. Surface reconciled in this bead.

title: testify: an audit finding in, the reason why out
spec: recount testify: read `pact audit --json` from stdin or --file; for every finding carrying (agent, ts) run the join and attach the transcript window
acceptance:
Reads `pact audit --json` from stdin or --file. For every finding carrying an agent and a timestamp, runs the join and attaches the transcript window and its tier. Emits the findings BACK OUT annotated, so it composes in a pipeline — this is what turns 'audit finding -> why' into one line.

Exit 0 when all findings were testified, 1 when some had no confident match AND the output lists which. An EMPTY findings set is exit 0: a clean audit is not a failure. Malformed input on stdin is a clean error, not a panic.

New command, so the cli-surface gate applies in full: --help, docs/cli.md's Commands block, generated completions, and scripts/check-docs.sh green in this bead.

title: fixtures and bench for everything v0.2.0 added
spec: synthetic subagents/ tree with a known keyed hit; keyed-id-with-absent-file refusal; model-agreement and model-discrepancy transcripts; a canned audit --json. Bench: keyed `at` must beat the topological path
acceptance:
Fixtures a human can verify by eye: a synthetic subagents/ tree with a keyed hit that is known by construction; a keyed id whose file is absent, asserting the NEW refusal reason and not merely exit 1; model-agreement and model-discrepancy transcripts; a canned `pact audit --json` for testify, including the empty-findings case.

Bench: keyed `at` must beat the topological path and land under 20 ms — it is a path join and a stat against a scan, so if it does not, the keyed path is not actually keyed. Added to the existing tests/bench.rs conventions (#[ignore], release, numbers printed with their conditions) without disturbing the two ceilings already there.

title: docs: the tier ladder, the chain, and what the harness still will not tell us
spec: both always reporting which tier answered and why the higher one did not
acceptance: docs/join.md gains the keyed tier above the existing four-rung ladder, the new refusal and its two causes, and — the part that matters — what the keyed tier does NOT fix: it only helps events written by an agent that knew its own id, so every pre-0.11.0 ledger, including recount's own 0.0.1, is un-keyed forever and falls to the topological tier with all its documented weakness. docs/connectors.md covers resolving a transcript by id and the model-per-turn finding. Both link the format-notes section on the self-id recipe rather than restating it.
